findings.description: SHEET-TAB-001 implies the Tax tab is a single flat per-entity band, just like Positions/Open Lots/Realized. The real code (sheets-view/src/lib.rs) instead splits the Tax *view* into two separate typed ranges: the accrual band published to TAX_TAB under TAX_HEADER (Sale ID, Lot ID, Jurisdiction, Tax Year, Amount, Lifecycle State), and a wholly distinct named range TAX_RESERVE_TAB = "Tax · Reserve Summary" under TAX_RESERVE_HEADER (Jurisdiction, Tax Year, Accrued, Moved, Paid, Outstanding, Shortfall) — the doc comments and the test `tax_accrual_band_has_no_among_data_summary_rows` make it a hard, tested invariant that the reserve summary never sits as rows inside the accrual band. All three A sketches missed this split entirely and modeled Tax as one flat per-position table (e.g. A3's `TaxEntry{symbol, term, short_gain, long_gain}`) — a sub-decision the EARS text gives no hint of, so all three independently invented the wrong shape. All three B reconstructions instead recovered the real two-band split near-verbatim (same tab name, same two header lists) and stated it as an explicit rule the given EARS text never mentions.

SHEET-TAB-001 only describes the static shape of one publish (header + per-entity rows, no summary rows) and says nothing about what a second/later publish does. The real code pins a specific republish contract: DATA_START_ROW = 2, and `SheetsViewClient::batch_update_view`'s doc contract (matched by the test `republish_regenerates_data_and_never_rewrites_frozen_header`) requires the header (row 1) be written exactly once and NEVER rewritten on republish, while only the data range from row 2 down is atomically rewritten and tail-truncated (a shrinking republish drops stale trailing rows). None of A1/A2/A3 modeled this header-immutable/data-range-only republish discipline — A3 even assumes the opposite by default ("`write_tab` fully replaces prior tab contents... rather than appending", with no carve-out preserving a frozen header separately from data). All three B reconstructions state the frozen-header + DATA_START_ROW + tail-truncate rule almost identically, again describing an enforced behavior the given EARS text is silent on.

All three B reconstructions describe, in close agreement, (a) the full workbook tab order that `workbook_tab_order()` enforces — the four view tabs, then History, then Tax Rules/Residency/Platforms & Aliases, then Ledger Events/Tax Events last, reasserted idempotently every republish (tests `workbook_order_views_then_config_then_logs_positions_landing`, `republish_idempotently_reasserts_tab_order`) — and (b) the defensive `ViewError::DuplicateSymbolRow(symbol)` guard in `render_positions` that rejects two rows for one symbol rather than emitting a duplicate. Neither is present in the given SHEET-TAB-001 text (which only covers the four tabs' internal per-entity-row shape), and none of the A sketches attempted either (out of scope of what the given spec text suggests), so this shows up only as a B-direction surfacing of enforced-but-unstated behavior — though it may legitimately belong to a sibling spec ID (e.g. a SHEET-LAYOUT-* requirement) not shown to us rather than being a true SHEET-TAB-001 gap.

A3 (only) invents a `set_read_only(&mut self, name: &str)` method on its `SheetsClient` trait and calls it as part of `publish_view_tabs`, modeling "read-only" as an explicit runtime protection call. The real `SheetsViewClient` trait has no such method (only `batch_update_view`, `set_tab_order`, `read_price_pass`, `write_stale_banner`) — "read-only" in the real design is purely a claim about the tabs being formula/value-driven and not meant for user edits, never enforced via a Sheets protected-range API. A1 and A2 both correctly guessed there is no such enforcement mechanism ("a contract, not a runtime guard"), so this is a minority (1-of-3) A-direction invention rather than a shared A/B gap.
